ayahOccurrences.text: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَقُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ ۖ إِنَّ قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَقُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ ۖ إِنَّ قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: لِدُلُوكِ is in the derivative form: دُلُوكٌ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
د/ل/ك   d–l–k to rub; to try, to gain experience, a well‐travelled camel, to be hard up; (of the sun) to pass the meridian, to set, to rise. Of this root, دُلُوكٌ dulūk occurs 1 time in the Qur’an
.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
دُلُوكٌ dulūk [v. n./n.] (of the sun) interpreted as: setting, inclining over the meridian, or rising ‏

(17:78) أَقِمِ الصَّلاَةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ إِلَى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ establish the prayer at the going down of the sun (or, at its crossing the zenith) until the darkness of the night.
